subject: general
question: In which of the following simple permanent tissues the cell walls are lignified?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a type of simple permanent tissue in plants that provides structural support and mechanical strength.
 
• The cell walls of sclerenchyma are heavily **lignified**, which means they are thickened by the deposition of lignin, making them hard and rigid.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are usually dead at maturity and lack protoplasm, allowing them to solely function in support.
 
• This tissue can be found in various parts of plants, such as stems, roots, veins of leaves, and hard shells of seeds and fruits.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are of two types: **fibers** (elongated cells) and **sclereids** (irregularly shaped cells). Both types have lignified walls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phloem:**

 
 
• Phloem is a complex permanent tissue involved in the transport of food in plants.
 
• It consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibers.
 
• While phloem fibers are lignified, the rest of the components are not, making the phloem not entirely lignified.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma:**
 
 
• Parenchyma is a simple permanent tissue composed of living cells with thin, non-lignified cell walls.
 
• It is involved in storage, photosynthesis, and secretion in plants.
 
• Examples include mesophyll cells in leaves and storage tissues in fruits.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• Collenchyma is a simple permanent tissue that provides mechanical support and flexibility to growing plant parts.
 
• Its cells have unevenly thickened walls made of cellulose and pectin, not lignin.
 
• It is found in leaf stalks, stems, and petioles.
 
 
 
• **Lignification:**
 
 
• Lignification is the process of depositing lignin in the cell walls, making them rigid and resistant to decay.
 
• Lignin is a complex organic polymer that is a key structural component of plant cell walls.
 
• This process is essential for the mechanical strength of tissues like sclerenchyma and xylem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of Sclerenchyma:**

 
 
• Fibers from sclerenchyma are used in making ropes, mats, and textiles (e.g., jute and coir).
 
• Sclereids contribute to the hardness of seed coats, fruit shells, and nuts.
 
 
 
• **Examples of lignified tissues:**
 
 
• Xylem vessels and tracheids, which are involved in water transport, are also lignified.
 
• These tissues, like sclerenchyma, provide structural support to plants.
